> छन्दः पादौ तु वेदस्य हस्तौ कल्पोऽथ उच्यते । ज्योतिषामयनं चक्षुर्निरुक्तं श्रोत्रमुच्यते ॥ शिक्षा घ्राणं तु वेदस्य मुखं व्याकरणं स्मृतम् । तस्मात्साङ्गमधीत्यैव ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥
> *chandaḥ pādau tu vedasya hastau kalpo'tha ucyate | jyotiṣām ayanaṃ cakṣur niruktaṃ śrotram ucyate || śikṣā ghrāṇaṃ tu vedasya mukhaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ smṛtam | tasmāt sāṅgam adhītyaiva brahmaloke mahīyate ||* (Panini Shiksha, verses 41-42)
>
> "**'Chhandas is the feet of the Veda, and Kalpa is declared to be its hands: Jyotisha is called its eye, and the Nirukta its ear. Śikṣā is the Veda's nose, Grammar they call its face: therefore he who studies the Veda along with these its limbs will be great in heaven.'**"

## Chapter 18. Why Knowledge of the Puranas, Nyaya, and Other Disciplines Is Necessary for Understanding the Veda's Meaning; and the Marks of One Unqualified to Receive That Knowledge

*Original title: "Vēdārthajñānakke Purāṇa-Nyāyādi itara vidyegaḷa jñānavu avaśyakavu — vēdārthajñānakke adhikāriyilladavana lakṣaṇagaḷu"*
**Printed pages 585–593 of the source.**

<div class="pgmark">original p. 585</div>

**Meaning:** for the Veda, Chandas is likened to its feet, Kalpa to its hands, Jyotiṣa to its eyes, Nirukta to its ears, Śikṣā to its nose, and Grammar is said to be its face. **Therefore, one who studies the Veda together with these six limbs is greatly honoured in the world of Brahma.**

### That the Puranas and Similar Texts, Together with the Fourteen Sources of Knowledge, Also Serve to Determine the Veda's Meaning

**That the Puranas, and similar texts, are, like the Angas, useful for a better understanding of the Veda, is recorded by Yajnavalkya:**

> पुराणन्यायमीमांसाधर्मशास्त्राङ्गमिश्रिताः । वेदाः स्थानानि विद्यानां धर्मस्य च चतुर्दश ॥
> *purāṇa-nyāya-mīmāṃsā-dharma-śāstrāṅga-miśritāḥ | vedāḥ sthānāni vidyānāṃ dharmasya ca caturdaśa ||* (Yajnavalkya Smriti 1-3)
>
> "**The Puranas, the Nyaya, Mimansa, and Dharma-shastras, the Vedas with their Angas, these be the fourteen sources of the sciences and of dharma.**"

**Elsewhere, too, it is thus recorded**—

<div class="pgmark">original p. 586</div>

**Now, in order to show that the Puranas and similar texts likewise serve to help determine the Veda's own meaning, Yajnavalkya himself states:**

> पुराणन्यायमीमांसाधर्मशास्त्राङ्गमिश्रिताः । वेदाः स्थानानि विद्यानां धर्मस्य च चतुर्दश ॥
> *purāṇa-nyāya-mīmāṃsā-dharma-śāstrāṅga-miśritāḥ | vedāḥ sthānāni vidyānāṃ dharmasya ca caturdaśa ||* (Yajnavalkya Smriti 1-3; see page 585 above)

**Meaning:** Puranas, Nyaya-shastra, Mimamsa, Dharma-shastra, and the Vedas together with their six Angas — mixed together — comprise the fourteen sources (sthāna) of both learning (vidyā) and dharma. And likewise in the Mahabharata—

> इतिहासपुराणाभ्यां वेदं समुपबृंहयेत् । बिभेत्यल्पश्रुताद्वेदो मामयं प्रहरिष्यति ॥
> *itihāsa-purāṇābhyāṃ vedaṃ samupabṛṃhayet | bibhety alpa-śrutād vedo mām ayaṃ prahariṣyati ||* (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 1-1-267)
>
> "**A man should strengthen the Veda by means of the Itihasas and Puranas: the Veda is afraid of the man of little learning, lest he should hurt it.**"

**Meaning:** history and purāṇic narrative should be used together to broaden and reinforce Vedic understanding. **The Veda [itself is described as] fearful of the man with little learning — apprehensive that such a person, through his limited understanding, might do it harm** [misinterpret or misapply it].

**The stories of Harishchandra, Nachiketa, and the like, told in the Aitareya, Taittiriya, Kathaka, and other Shakhas, which are useful for the better understanding both of dharma and of brahma, are explained in the Itihasa books.** The statements found in the Upanishads concerning the creation, the preservation, and the absorption of the world are explained in the Brahma, Padma, Vaishnava, and other Puranas. **Compare the well-known verse, "Sargaśca pratisargaśca."**

**Meaning:** Itihasa and Purana strengthen and confirm the meaning found within the Veda. It should be understood that ancient and traditional matters — the Veda's own supporting narrative context — are made firm through these Itihasas and Puranas. Since the Veda is described as fearful of one whose learning is shallow, this indicates: if a person with little genuine understanding grasps only the surface meaning of the Veda (its own scriptural expression), he may inadvertently do it harm through misapplication — this is what is meant here.

<div class="pgmark">original p. 587</div>

**The hymns of the Aitareya, Taittiriya, Kāṭhaka and other Shakhas and the tales of Harishchandra, Nachiketa and others are useful for teaching dharma and the nature of Brahma, and all these are set out at length in the Itihasa books. The matters of creation, preservation and dissolution of the world spoken of in the Upanishads (and in some hymns of the Rigveda too) are described in great detail, and plainly, in the Brahma, Padma, Vaishnava and other Puranas. Those who know the Puranas say that these are the matters chiefly to be described in them**—

> सर्गश्च प्रतिसर्गश्च वंशो मन्वन्तराणि च । वंशानुचरितं चेति पुराणं पञ्चलक्षणम् ॥
> *sargaś ca pratisargaś ca vaṃśo manvantarāṇi ca | vaṃśānucaritaṃ ceti purāṇaṃ pañca-lakṣaṇam ||* (Vishnu Purana 3-6-25; Amarakosha 1-6-5)

**Meaning:** creation (sarga), re-creation [after periodic dissolution] (pratisarga), dynastic genealogy (vaṃśa), the ages of the Manus (manvantara), and dynastic history (vaṃśānucharita) — these are the five defining characteristics of a Purana.

**Since creation and the like are described at length in the Puranas, they can be learnt from them.**

**Nyaya-shastra treats of sixteen categories — pramāṇa (valid means of knowledge), prameya, saṃśaya (doubt), prayojana, dṛṣṭānta and so on — and by following it one can decide that a given text is authoritative in this sense and not in that.**

**How the Purva and Uttara Mimamsas help to a better understanding of the Vedas is clear enough.**

**In the Smritis of Manu, Atri, Vishnu, Harita, and other writers, injunctions found in the Vedas, such for example as that concerning the evening prayer, are extended and developed.** The text "**tad u ha va ete brahmavādinaḥ pūrvābhimukhāḥ sandhyābhivādaya gāyatrī-bhimantritā apa ūrdhvaṃ vikṣipanti**," and similar, is a command to say the evening prayer. That other, "**pañca vā ete mahāyajñāḥ satataṃ pravartante**," is a command to perform the so-called great sacrifices. Other instances of commands given in the Veda and developed in the Smritis can be found.

**Since in this way the Puranas are a help to a better understanding of the Veda, the name "vidyāsthāna" (strongholds of wisdom) is rightly, in Yajnavalkya's verse above, applied to them.**

<div class="pgmark">original p. 588</div>

> तदु ह वा एते ब्रह्मवादिनः पूर्वाभिमुखाः संध्यायां गायत्रीयाभिमन्त्रिता अप ऊर्ध्वं विक्षिपन्ति ॥
> *tad u ha vā ete brahmavādinaḥ pūrvābhimukhāḥ saṃdhyāyāṃ gāyatrīyābhimantritā apa ūrdhvaṃ vikṣipanti ||* (Taittiriya Aranyaka 2-2-2)

**Meaning: this is what is stated** — those who know brahma, facing east, at twilight-time, consecrate the [sacred water] with the Gayatri mantra and then cast it upward, toward the sun as it rises before them (that is, [perform] the "arghya"-offering) — this is the specific procedure enjoined for the twilight-prayer.

**And also**: "**Pañca vā ete mahāyajñāḥ satataṃ pravartante**" (Taittiriya Aranyaka 2-10) — this and similar [texts], declared as commands, establish the requirement to continually perform the [five] great sacrifices. In this way, the same procedures found here and there [in various Vedic texts] are elaborated more fully in various Smritis; a careful study of both together allows one to properly grasp these matters.

**Since in the manner stated above the Puranas and the rest are also helps to a right understanding of the Veda's meaning, it is proper to call them "vidyā" (sources of learning).**

**These fourteen sources of learning that begin with the Puranas are the four Vedas, the six Angas, the Puranas, Nyaya-shastra, Mimamsa and Dharma-shastra: they are the fountain-head of all the sciences and of dharma; that is, the other sciences have come forth in accordance with them. Since these fourteen are helps to understanding the meaning of the Veda, who is qualified (adhikārin) to take hold of them? That such a qualified person exists is shown by four mantras from different Shakhas, which Yaska quotes (Nirukta 2-4).**

**The first is this:**

> विद्या ह वै ब्राह्मणमाजगाम गोपाय मा शेवधिष्टेऽहमस्मि । असूयकायानृजवेऽनृतायाशीलाय मा ब्रूया वीर्यवती तथा स्याम् ॥
> *vidyā ha vai brāhmaṇam ājagāma gopāya mā śevadhis te'ham asmi | asūyakāyānṛjave'nṛtāyāśīlāya mā brūyā vīryavatī tathā syām ||* (Nirukta 2-4)
>
> "**Wisdom came to the brahmin and said, 'Protect me for I am your treasure: do not teach me to the scornful or the knavish or the sensual man; so shall I be strong.'**"

<div class="pgmark">original p. 589</div>

> विद्याभिमानिनी देवता ब्राह्मणमुपदेष्टारमाचार्यमाजगाम । आगत्य चैवं प्रार्थयामास हे ब्राह्मण मामवनद्धिकारिणेच्छन्दुरुषार्थेच्छुरस्मि । तादृश्यं तुभ्यं तदुपदेष्टरि त्वयि च योग्यमूनं करोमि । यत्खार्जनेन विद्यां नाभ्यर्जते विद्यां नाभ्यर्जते यश्च मनोदन्धाचारनियतो न भवति । तादृशे भव्यक्ष्यशिक्षाभावेभ्यो मां न ब्रूयात् । तथा सति तव हृदये स्थित्वा फलप्रदा भवेयम् ॥
> *vidyābhimāninī devatā brāhmaṇam upadeṣṭāram ācāryam ājagāma | āgatya caivaṃ prārthayāmāsa he brāhmaṇa mām avanaddhikāriṇecchan durūṣārthecchur asmi | tādṛśyaṃ tubhyaṃ tad-upadeṣṭari tvayi ca yogyam ūnaṃ karomi | yat khārjanena vidyāṃ nābhyarjate vidyāṃ nābhyarjate yaś ca mano-dhandhācāra-niyato na bhavati | tādṛśe bhavyakṣyaśikṣā-bhāvebhyo māṃ na brūyāt | tathā sati tava hṛdaye sthitvā phala-pradā bhaveyam ||*

**Meaning:** the goddess who is immanent in all learning came to the brahmin teacher, that is, to the Acharya, and thus besought him: "O brahmin! protect me, do not teach me to him that is unworthy. I am for a treasure to you, giving you all that a man can desire. He that does despite to me, your benefactress, or to you who teach me — he that does not follow learning uprightly, he that does not keep his body under by due observance of the rules about bathing, rinsing the mouth, and the like before lessons — to all such pupils, who are pupils in appearance only, do not teach me. So shall I abide in your heart and bear fruit."

**Next the second verse.**

> यमात्मने कुर्वते नित्यं संप्रयच्छन्नमृतं वदति । तं मन्येते पितरं मातरं च तस्मै न द्रुह्येत्कतमच्चनाहः ॥
> *yam ātmane kurvate nityaṃ samprayacchann amṛtaṃ vadati | taṃ manyete pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca tasmai na druhyet katamac canāhaḥ ||* (Nirukta 2-4)

**"He who fills the ears with truth, but not so as to hurt, and who adds thereto nectar, he is the pupil's father and mother, and should in no wise be injured by him."**

<div class="pgmark">original p. 590</div>

**Meaning:** the first verse contained a prohibitory rule for the teacher: this has one for the pupil. By "**सत्य**" (*satya*, "truth") is meant the Veda, called so as being the opposite of worldly talk, which is untrue, and not conducive to man's chief end. **"यमात्मने कुर्वते नित्यम्"** (*yam ātmane kurvate nityaṃ*) — the teacher who completely fills his pupil's ears with the words of the Veda. The root "**तृणत्ति**" (*tṛṇatti*, to fill/pierce), by the force of its prefix "**सम्**" (*sam*), and from the context, takes a meaning different from the usual one. The meaning is "whoever recites the Veda to him." How? **"अमृतं वदति"** (*amṛtaṃ vadati*) — so as not to give him pain. If the boy be dull and unable to learn a verse or a half verse at a time, the teacher, in order to avoid giving him...

**This is the meaning of the second mantra: in the first mantra the teacher was given the rules he is to follow in teaching the Veda; this mantra states the pupil's duties. The word the original uses for "true" is the negative of "vitatha"; "vitatha" is an untrue utterance from which no human end is gained, that is, the sentences used in worldly dealings; the opposite, "avitatha", is the true Vedic utterance that serves the human end. With such Vedic words, nectar in nature, the teacher fills the pupil's ears, that is, he always teaches him; here, by the force of the prefix, another sense must be given to the root meaning "to fill": he who always makes the pupil hear the Veda. And if the pupil is dull-witted, that is, unable to take in even half a Rik or a Rik, he teaches him a pāda of the Rik, or a part of a pāda, according to his power of understanding, so that no trouble is caused to him.**

<div class="pgmark">original p. 591</div>

**pain, makes him learn the fourth part of a verse, or even the eighth part. What more?** "**Adding thereto nectar**." By "nectar" is meant the sense of the Veda, as distinguished from the new words. Because it makes a man a god, or procures for him final release. "Adding thereto nectar" means giving him that. **Such a teacher, the pupil, who is a pupil indeed, must regard as his chief father and mother. Why are his father and mother according to the flesh not chief? Because they gave him at his first birth his worthless fleshly body only. The pupil must not injure in any way whatever his teacher, who is thus in the highest sense his father and his mother.**

**Manu himself, in his own Smriti, establishes this meaning in the following verse—**

> उत्पादकब्रह्मदातोर्गरीयान् ब्रह्मदः पिता । ब्रह्मजन्म हि विप्रस्य प्रेत्य चेह च शाश्वतम् ॥
> *utpādaka-brahmadātor garīyān brahmadaḥ pitā | brahma-janma hi viprasya pretya ceha ca śāśvatam ||* (Manu Smriti 2-145)
>
> "Between the natural father and the giver of sacred learning, the giver of sacred learning is the more venerable father; for the birth through the Veda is eternal, both here and hereafter, for the brahmin."

**Next the third verse.**

> अध्यापिता ये गुरुं नाद्रियन्ते विप्रा वाचा मनसा कर्मणा वा । युष्मैव ते न गुरोर्भोज्यनीया स्तस्यैव ताज्ज्ञप्ति शृतं तदिति ॥
> *adhyāpitā ye guruṃ nādriyante viprā vācā manasā karmaṇā vā | yuṣmaiva te na guror bhojanīyā stasyaiva tāj jñaptiḥ śrutaṃ tad iti ||* (Nirukta 2-4)
>
> "**But those brahmins who have received instruction, yet do not honour their teacher in thought, word, and deed, as they ought — not to be protected by their teacher, so neither will the holy revelation which they have learned protect them.**"

**Meaning:** those brahmin students who, having received instruction from their teacher regarding the Veda's meaning, do not thereafter honour him through mind, speech, and bodily action — such students should not be [further] taught or supported by their teacher. And since these students fail to properly honour their teacher, the Veda's own knowledge that they have thus far received will not, in the end, genuinely protect them or bear fruit for them.

<div class="pgmark">original p. 592</div>

**Meaning [continuing the third verse's explanation]:** among those who have engaged in the study of the Veda's meaning and made effort to understand it thoroughly, some, out of disrespect toward their teacher, disregard his instruction, do not honour his wishes, and behave with contempt toward him. Such disciples, though outwardly appearing to be genuine students of their teacher, are not so in the eyes of wise men. Since these students fail in their proper duty toward the teacher, the Vedic knowledge they've received will not ultimately protect or benefit them.

> **"Those wicked brahmins, who after having been taught do not honour their teacher by respectful language, thought for his interests and obedience to his commands, are his pupils in appearance only, and ought not to be protected by him. They are unworthy of his favour: he will not have compassion on them. And as he will not protect them, so neither will the Veda, which he has taught them, protect these wicked pupils. It will not bear them fruit."**

**Next the fourth verse.**

> यमेव विद्याः शुचिमप्रमत्तं मेधाविनं ब्रह्मचर्योपपन्नम् । यस्मै न द्रुह्येत्तस्मैचनाह तस्मै मा ब्रूया निधिपाय ब्रह्म ॥
> *yam eva vidyāḥ śucim apramattaṃ medhāvinaṃ brahmacaryopapannam | yasmai na druhyet tasmai canāha tasmai mā brūyā nidhipāya brahma ||* (Nirukta 2-4)
>
> "**But if there be one whom you know to be pure, eager to hear, intelligent, and chaste, who will never do you harm, teach me to him, Oh brahmin! he will protect me, your treasure.**"

**Meaning [Sayana's summary]:** O Acharya, to that chief pupil whom you know to be pure and possessed of such virtues, who never does you harm, is devoted to your service, intelligent, free from laziness and unfailing in the rules of brahmacharya — to him teach me, the knowledge of the Veda that is your treasure. Such a student will indeed protect me, [Vidya herself says,] your treasure, and preserve the Veda's own meaning faithfully.

**॥ Iti Sāyaṇācārya-kṛtā Ṛgveda-Bhāṣya-Bhūmikā Samāptā ॥**

**॥ इति सायणाचार्यकृता ऋग्वेदभाष्यभूमिका समाप्ता ॥**

**"Thus ends the Rigveda-Bhashya-Bhumika, composed by Sayanacharya."**

**This marks the formal close of Sayana's introductory preface (Bhumika) to his Rigveda commentary.** What follows next, according to the chapter opening below, is the beginning of the discussion proper on the mantra's own defining characteristics — turning at last from the preface's extensive philosophical program (spanning the Veda's nature, the mantra/brahmana distinction, the authority debates, the Angas, and the qualifications of student and teacher) to the commentary's actual verse-by-verse work.

<div class="pgmark">original p. 593</div>

### Final Page of the Bhūmikā

**Meaning:** teach me, your treasure (the knowledge of the Veda), to that chief pupil who is pure, endowed with humility and other virtues, who never does you harm, devoted to your service, intelligent, free from laziness and unfailing in the rules of brahmacharya. O revered one, such a good pupil will preserve the knowledge you teach. **In this way, having made her request that the teacher, upon finding a worthy and virtuous student who faithfully observes the discipline, should teach him the knowledge of the Veda, Manu Smriti gives this very verse**—

> यमेव तु शुचिं विद्यान्नियतं ब्रह्मचारिणम् । तस्मै वां ब्रूहि विप्राय निधिं कामप्रवादिने ॥
> *yam eva tu śuciṃ vidyān niyataṃ brahmacāriṇam | tasmai vāṃ brūhi viprāya nidhiṃ kāma-pravādine ||* (Manu Smriti 2-115; Nirukta 2-4)

**"O Teacher, teach me wisdom in the form of the Veda. To him whom you know to be a pupil indeed, pure, eager to hear, intelligent, and chaste, and who will never do you harm: he will protect your treasure. At such a request made to him by the Goddess of learning, the teacher will teach him, who is a pupil indeed, the knowledge of the Veda."**

**Therefore we will now explain the Rig-Veda in accordance with its six Angas.**

**इल्लिगे सायणाचार्यरिंद रचितवाद ऋग्वेदभाष्यभूमिकेयु समाप्तवादुदु.**

**ಇಲ್ಲಿಗೆ ಸಾಯಣಾಚಾರ್ಯರಿಂದ ರಚಿತವಾದ ಋಗ್ವೇದಭಾಷ್ಯಭೂಮಿಕೆಯು ಸಮಾಪ್ತವಾದುದು.**

**"Here ends the Rigveda-Bhashya-Bhumika, composed by Sayanacharya."**

**॥ ಶ್ರೀರಸ್ತು ॥**

**॥ Śrī Rastu ॥**

**"May there be auspiciousness."**

# PART III: The Ṛgveda Saṃhitā with Sāyaṇa's Commentary (Mādhavīya Vedārtha-Prakāśa)

## Title Page

*(The page opens with a decorative sunburst medallion enclosing the syllable ॐ (Om), inscribed above with:)*

**॥ श्री गणाधिपतये नमः ॥**
*Śrī Gaṇādhipataye Namaḥ*
"Salutations to the Lord of the Gaṇas [Ganesha]."

**अथ श्रीसायणाचार्यविरचिता माधवीय वेदार्थप्रकाश संहिता।**
*Atha Śrī-Sāyaṇācārya-viracitā Mādhavīya Vedārtha-prakāśa Saṃhitā |*
"Now [begins] the Mādhavīya Vedārtha-prakāśa Saṃhitā, composed by the illustrious Sāyaṇācārya."

**अस्माभिः विद्वन्निरचितकर्णाटकभाषानुवादयुता**
*asmābhiḥ vidvan-nirachita-karṇāṭaka-bhāṣānuvāda-yutā*
"— accompanied by a Kannada-language translation composed by this humble scholar —"

**ऋग्वेदसंहिता**
*Ṛgveda Saṃhitā*
"The Rigveda Samhita"

**॥ प्रथमं मण्डलम् ॥**
*Prathamaṃ Maṇḍalam*
"Book One (Maṇḍala I)"

### Invocation

> ॐ वागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे । यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युः स्मृत्वा वन्दे तमादिगणम् ॥
> *oṃ vāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānām upakrame | yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syuḥ smṛtvā vande tam ādigaṇam ||*
>
> "At the outset of every undertaking, the wise — Bṛhaspati (Lord of Speech) and others — having bowed to whom become accomplished in their aims: remembering him, I too salute that same foremost of the Gaṇas [Ganesha]."

Śrī Sāyaṇācārya, in his Rigveda-Bhāṣya-Bhūmikā, having extensively examined — with the help of works such as Mīmāṃsā, Vyākaraṇa, and Dharma-shāstra — many profound topics (the Veda's defining characteristics, the Veda's authority, the Veda's non-human origin, the matter of Vedic study, the subject-matter the Veda expounds, a close exposition of the Vedāṅgas, who is qualified to receive Vedic knowledge, and so on), now, before beginning this Vedic commentary proper, briefly states — as an introductory matter — both the division-scheme of the Aṣṭaka-adhyāyas found in the Rigveda, and the matter of the mantras' ritual application (viniyoga), and thus opens the treatise itself.

> तदर्थमृग्वेदोक्तार्थः षडङ्गानुसारेण व्याख्यायते । मन्त्रब्राह्मणात्मके वेदे ब्राह्मणस्य मन्त्रव्याख्यानोपयोगित्वादादौ ब्राह्मणमारभ्य काण्डशः व्याख्यातम् । अथ तत्र तत्र ब्राह्मणोदाहरणेन मन्त्राख्यः संहिताग्रन्थो व्याख्यातव्यः ॥
> *tad-artham ṛgvedokta-arthaḥ ṣaḍ-aṅgānusāreṇa vyākhyāyate | mantra-brāhmaṇātmake vede brāhmaṇasya mantra-vyākhyānopayogitvād ādau brāhmaṇam ārabhya kāṇḍaśaḥ vyākhyātam | atha tatra tatra brāhmaṇodāharaṇena mantrākhyaḥ saṃhitā-granthaḥ vyākhyātavyaḥ ||*
>
> "For this purpose, the sense stated in the Rigveda is expounded following the six Aṅgas. Since, in the Veda — which consists of mantra and brāhmaṇa together — the Brāhmaṇa is useful for explaining the mantra, [the commentary] has been expounded section by section (kāṇḍaśaḥ), beginning first with the Brāhmaṇa. Now, citing the Brāhmaṇa at each relevant point, the Saṃhitā-text — that is, the mantras — is to be expounded."

Up to this point, in the Bhāṣya-Bhūmikā, we have broached many topics; at its close we discussed who is qualified for the Veda — that is, who should undertake to know the Veda and its meaning? What qualities should such a person possess? In what manner should study be undertaken?

<div class="pgmark">original p. 596</div>

What is the way of understanding the meaning? Which auxiliary works are needed for it? In what manner is the meaning to be explained? — all these matters have been explained. Now we shall begin to expound the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā in accordance with the six Angas, that is, with their help.

**That the Veda consists of mantra and brahmana has already been stated.** In explaining the mantra-portion the Brahmana is essential, and therefore the Brahmana (the Aitareya Brahmana) was first commented on, together with the Aranyaka (the Aitareya Aranyaka). Now the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, which consists of mantras, is to be commented on, together with examples of Brahmana passages suited to each place.

> स चाग्निमीळ इत्यारभ्य यथा वः सुसातेत्यन्तोऽष्टकाण्ड्ये दशमण्डलेऽष्टाध्यायैः पञ्चाशीत्यनुवाकैः सहस्राधिकसूक्त्या द्विसहस्राधिकवर्गया दशसहस्राधिकर्क्संख्यया ऋग्भ्योऽपेतः । तस्य च ग्रन्थस्य कृत्स्नस्यास्यामाम्नातक्रमेणैव सामान्यविनियोगो ब्रह्मयज्ञपाठपूर्वमेवाभिहितः । विशेषविनियोगस्तु कतौ सूत्रकारेण प्रदर्शितः । स च त्रिविधः । सूक्तविनियोगस्त्वचादिषड्विनियोग एकैकस्या ऋचो विनियोगश्चेति ॥
> *sa cāgnimīḷa ity ārabhya yathā vaḥ susāteti-anto'ṣṭakāṇḍye daśa-maṇḍale'ṣṭādhyāyaiḥ pañcāśīty-anuvākaiḥ sahasrādhika-sūktyā dvisahasrādhika-vargayā daśasahasrādhika-ṛk-saṃkhyayā ṛgbhyo'petaḥ | tasya ca granthasya kṛtsnasyāsyām āmnāta-krameṇaiva sāmānya-viniyogo brahma-yajña-pāṭha-pūrvam evābhihitaḥ | viśeṣa-viniyogas tu katau sūtra-kāreṇa pradarśitaḥ | sa ca trividhaḥ | sūkta-viniyogas tv acādi-ṣaḍ-viniyoga ekaikasyā ṛco viniyogaś ceti ||* *(the precise digits in this dense enumeration were read with care but the scan resolution leaves a couple of them, noted below, less than fully certain)*
>
> "That [Samhita], beginning with 'agnimīḷe' and ending with 'yathā vaḥ susāte,' is furnished, in the eight-Ashtaka division, with ten Maṇḍalas, sixty-four (eight-times-eight) Adhyāyas, eighty-five Anuvākas, a little over one thousand Sūktas, a little over two thousand Vargas, and a little over ten thousand Ṛks. The general application (sāmānya-viniyoga) of this entire text, in its own recited sequence, has already been stated in connection with the Brahma-yajña recitation. The specific application (viśeṣa-viniyoga), however, has been shown by the Sūtra-authors in the ritual texts themselves. This specific application is of three kinds: application of a whole Sūkta, application of a group of six verses beginning with a given one (ācādi-ṣaḍ), and application of a single Ṛk individually."

**Meaning:** the Rigveda Samhita we are about to expound begins with "**agnimīḷe**" and ends with "**yathā vaḥ susāte**." We have already described this division-scheme of the Rigveda earlier (see page 11). In total, the Rigveda Samhita is divided into eight **Ashtakas**, and each Ashtaka is further divided into eight **Adhyayas**. The number of **Vargas** within each Adhyaya, however, is not uniform — where shorter-syllabled meters such as Gayatri predominate, that Adhyaya contains more Vargas; where longer-syllabled meters such as Jagati predominate, that Adhyaya contains fewer Vargas. The overall length of each Adhyaya thus remains roughly, though not perfectly, equal. Following this scheme, the Rigveda has **sixty-four Adhyayas** in total (eight Ashtakas × eight Adhyayas each). This arrangement was established for ease of study and has been followed since ancient times.

**The Mandala-division-scheme is a different system** — older than the Ashtaka-scheme. Following the lineages of the mantra-seeing rishis, each Mandala generally contains mantras "seen" (dṛṣṭa) by one principal rishi together with his descendants or disciples. The Rigveda contains **ten such Mandalas**. Maṇḍalas 1, 9 and 10 do not follow this order: they contain mantras seen by many rishis; this has been discussed earlier.

**Therefore, it is said that the Rigveda contains:** eight Ashtakas, ten Mandalas, sixty-four Adhyayas, eighty-five Anuvakas, a little more than one thousand Suktas, a little more than two thousand Vargas, and more than ten thousand Riks (verses).

<div class="pgmark">original p. 597</div>

Although we have already stated the division of the Veda earlier, it is necessary in the present context to state one or two matters on this subject briefly.

> प्रत्यक्षेणानुमित्या वा यस्तूपायो न बुध्यते । एतं विन्दन्ति वेदेन तस्माद्वेदस्य वेदता ॥
> *pratyakṣeṇānumityā vā yas tūpāyo na budhyate | etaṃ vindanti vedena tasmād vedasya vedatā ||* (see earlier discussion in the Bhūmikā, under the Nirukta Aṅga)
>
> "That means [of knowledge] which cannot be grasped either through direct perception or through inference — this alone is made known through the Veda; therefore the Veda derives its very name 'Veda' [from the root vid, 'to know']."

**Meaning:** whatever cannot be established through the ordinary means of knowledge — direct perception or inference — is made knowable solely through the Veda; it is for this reason that "the Veda" bears the very name "Veda," from the root "vid" (to know), signifying that which makes known what is otherwise unknowable.

**As stated in the Puranas and similar texts:** the Rigveda has **twenty-one (21)** shakha-divisions; the Yajurveda has **one hundred and one (101)** shakha-divisions (of these, Shukla-Yajurveda has fifteen shakhas, and Krishna-Yajurveda has eighty-six shakhas, together making 101); the Samaveda has a **thousand** shakhas; and the Atharvaveda has **nine** shakhas. Of these many shakhas, a great number have been lost over the course of time and are no longer in use today — only a few are still available.

**Every Veda comprises two kinds of portions:** the mantra-portion (Samhita) and the Brahmana-portion. The sage Apastamba says:

> मन्त्रे ब्राह्मणयोर्वेदनामधेयम् ।
> *mantre brāhmaṇayor veda-nāmadheyam |*
> "'Veda' is the name applied to mantra and Brahmana together."

The 21 shakhas of the Rigveda can be divided into five main groups: Ashvalayana, Sankhayana, Shakala, Bashkala and Mandukeya. Of these five, we have now undertaken to comment on the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā of the Ashvalayana shakha.

The division of this Ṛgveda-saṃhitā is of two kinds. The first is by maṇḍala, anuvāka, sūkta and ṛk; the second is by aṣṭaka, adhyāya, varga and ṛk. The first division is convenient for use in sacrifices and the like; the second is convenient for study, that is, for learning the Veda. In this Rigveda there are hymns to deities such as Agni, Vayu, Indra, Mitra-Varuna, Usha, Bhaga and Vishnu, and in these hymns the qualities, acts and so on of the respective deities are described; therefore these mantras are useful in sacrifices and similar rites. In particular, in the first hymn of the first adhyaya of the first ashtaka of this Rik-samhita, Agni is praised; therefore this hymn is called the hymn of Agni. Before reciting the hymns or mantras of the Rigveda, the rishi, deity and metre of each must be stated, so the rule runs. The rishi, deity and metre of the hymns and the rest are set out fully in the Anukramanika; the commentator too states the rishi, deity and metre at the beginning of his commentary on each hymn. Although the application (viniyoga) of the mantras is stated in the Shrauta-sutras and the like, the commentator briefly states the application of the mantras as they occur from place to place.

Though there are many metres, they are divided into three main classes. In the first class there are seven principal metres — **Gāyatrī, Uṣṇik, Anuṣṭubh, Bṛhatī, Paṅkti, Triṣṭubh, and Jagatī** — the...

<div class="pgmark">original p. 598</div>

**These are the principal meters.** Each meter has many sub-varieties, which we have already explained at length with examples earlier (see p. 222). The seven meters mentioned above, beginning with Gayatri, have respectively **24, 28, 32, 36, 40, 44, 48** syllables.

**In the second group** — **अतिजगती, शक्करी, अतिशक्करी, अष्टिः, अत्यष्टिः, धृतिः, अतिधृतिः** (*Atijagatī, Śakvarī, Atiśakvarī, Aṣṭiḥ, Atyaṣṭiḥ, Dhṛtiḥ, Atidhṛtiḥ*) — these seven meters have respectively **52, 56, 60, 64, 68, 72, 76** syllables.

**In the third group** — **कृतिः, प्रकृतिः, आकृतिः, विकृतिः, संकृतिः, अभिकृतिः, उत्कृतिः** (*Kṛtiḥ, Prakṛtiḥ, Ākṛtiḥ, Vikṛtiḥ, Saṃkṛtiḥ, Abhikṛtiḥ, Utkṛtiḥ*) — these seven meters have respectively **80, 84, 88, 92, 96, 100, 104** syllables.

**When stating the totals for Ashtakas, Adhyayas, Vargas, and the rest, the Bhashyakara [Sayana] does not give an exact figure, but instead uses the general expression "**ईषदधिक**" (*īṣad-adhika*, "a little more than").** This is because — although the counts of Mandala, Anuvaka, Ashtaka, and Adhyaya are not disputed — genuine differences of opinion exist regarding the counts of Suktas, Vargas, and mantras (Riks). For example: in the eighth Maṇḍala, Sūktas 49–59 are called **Vālakhilya-sūktas**; these eleven Vālakhilya-sūktas are absent from some shakhas' texts. Some include these **khila-sūktas** (supplementary hymns) within the Samhita; others do not. This is why differences arise in the count of Suktas.

**Regarding the count of Vargas:** generally, a group of roughly five Riks is treated as one Varga. If a Sukta contains 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 or 7 Riks, that entire Sukta itself is counted as a single Varga. A Sukta containing 8 Riks is treated by some as a single Varga, and by others as two Vargas. This too causes differences in the Varga-count.

**Regarding the count of Riks:** in many places there occur Riks in the "**dvipadā virāṭ**" meter. Some scholars count these as Riks having two padas (that is, half of a full Rik), while others hold that "dvipadā" is merely the meter's own name, and that — like every other meter — it too actually comprises four padas in full. According to the first view, two padas (half a Rik) count as one whole Rik; according to the second view, four padas (a complete first-half plus second-half) count as one Rik. This too is a source of variation in the total Rik-count. **Taking all of this into account, the Bhashyakara generally states the Varga and related counts using the qualifier "īṣad-adhika" (a little more than), rather than an exact figure.**

**Now let us examine the matter of the mantras' application (viniyoga).** Viniyoga means: the rule that a given mantra should be employed in a given ritual context. Since mantras are used according to the specific rite being performed, viniyoga is thus tied to that rite (karma). This scheme of application is of two kinds: **general (sāmānya)** and **specific (viśeṣa)**. Reciting all the mantras of this Rigveda Samhita in their entirety — as in the Brahma-yajna, japa, complete recitation (pārāyaṇa), and similar practices — is called the mantras' **"general application."** In yajnas and other rites, and likewise in other ritual observances — that is, in the japa and similar practices undertaken to realize one's chosen deity — the [specific] application...

<div class="pgmark">original p. 599</div>

...belonging to each individual mantra is determined. This specific application is itself of three kinds: application of a whole Sukta, application of a group of three Riks, and application of a single Rik.

> तत्राग्निमीळ इति सूक्तं प्रातरनुवाक आग्नेये क्रतौ विनियुक्तम् । स विनियोग आश्वलायनेन चतुर्थाध्यायस्य त्रयोदशे खण्डे सूत्रितः । आवा नो अग्न इति षळग्निमीळेऽग्निं दूतमिति । तत्र हीनपादग्रहणात्सूक्तनिश्चयः । सूक्तं सूक्तादौ हीने पादे । आ. १-१ । इति परिभाषितत्वात् । तस्मिन्सूक्ते प्रथमाया ऋचो द्वितीयस्यां पवमानेष्टौ स्विष्टकृतो याज्यात्वेन विनियोगः । स च द्वितीयाध्यायस्य प्रथमखण्डे सूत्रितः । साह्वान्विश्वा अभियुजोऽग्निमीळे पुरोहितमिति संयाज्ये इति । तत्र कृत्स्नपादग्रहणादृगित्यवगम्यते । ऋचं पादग्रहणे आ. १-१ । इति परिभाषितत्वात् । तथा संयाज्ये इत्युक्ते सौविष्टकृती प्रतीयात् आ. २-१ । इति परिभाषितत्वात्स्विष्टकृत्संबन्धनिश्चयः । तत्रापि द्वितीयमन्त्रत्वेनोदाहृतत्वाद्याज्यात्वम् । यद्यपि साह्वानित्यनया पुरोनुवाक्ययैव देवताया अनुस्मरणरूपसंस्कारः सिद्धस्तथापि याज्यानुवाक्ययोः समुच्चयो द्वादशेऽध्याये चतुर्थपादे मीमांसितः ॥
> *tatrāgnimīḷa iti sūktaṃ prātaranuvāka āgneye kratau viniyuktam | sa viniyoga āśvalāyanena caturthādhyāyasya trayodaśe khaṇḍe sūtritaḥ | āvā no agna iti ṣaḷ agnim īḷe'gniṃ dūtam iti | tatra hīnapāda-grahaṇāt sūkta-niścayaḥ | sūktaṃ sūktādau hīne pāde | Ā. 1-1 | iti paribhāṣitatvāt | tasmin sūkte prathamāyā ṛco dvitīyasyāṃ pavamāneṣṭau sviṣṭakṛto yājyātvena viniyogaḥ | sa ca dvitīyādhyāyasya prathamakhaṇḍe sūtritaḥ | sāhvān viśvā abhiyujo'gnim īḷe purohitam iti saṃyājye iti | tatra kṛtsnapāda-grahaṇād ṛg ity avagamyate | ṛcaṃ pādagrahaṇe Ā. 1-1 | iti paribhāṣitatvāt | tathā saṃyājye ity ukte sauviṣṭakṛtī pratīyāt Ā. 2-1 | iti paribhāṣitatvāt sviṣṭakṛt-saṃbandha-niścayaḥ | tatrāpi dvitīya-mantratvenodāhṛtatvād yājyātvam | yadyapi sāhvān ity anayā puronuvākyayaiva devatāyā anusmaraṇa-rūpa-saṃskāraḥ siddhas tathāpi yājyānuvākyayoḥ samuccayo dvādaśe'dhyāye caturthapāde mīmāṃsitaḥ ||*
>
> "There, the sukta 'agnimīḷe' is applied by him [Ashvalayana] to the Āgneya rite within the Prātar-anuvāka. This application is laid down by Āśvalāyana in the thirteenth section of the fourth Adhyāya [of his Shrauta-sutra]."

**In the relevant context**, since the "**agnim īḷe**" sukta is recited within the ritual (kratu) belonging to the **Prātar-anuvāka** (morning-recitation) portion, this constitutes the prescribed application (viniyoga) for this sukta.

**In the Soma-yaga**, on the night preceding the pressing-day (sutyā-dina), from midnight until dawn, three deities — **Agni, Uṣas, and the Aśvin-deities** — are praised using the seven meters beginning with Gāyatrī. The act of praising a particular deity in this way is called the **"kratu"** connected with that deity: praising Agni is the **Āgneya-kratu**; praising Uṣas is the **Auṣasya-kratu**; praising the Aśvins is the **Āśvina-kratu** — these are the three kratus [of this section]. Since these are recited a little before dawn, this rite as a whole is called the **Prātar-anuvāka** (the morning recitation). Within this Prātar-anuvāka, when performing the Āgneya-kratu — that is, when reciting the Agni-related sukta — this very sukta, "**agnim īḷe**," is recited. **This is precisely the application (viniyoga) of this sukta.**

Āśvalāyana, in a sūtra of the thirteenth khaṇḍa of the fourth adhyāya of his Śrauta-sūtra, states: "**āvā no agna iti ṣaḍ agnim īḷe'gniṃ dūtam**" — this is the application of this sūkta. When discussing the application of the mantras within his sutra, Ashvalayana refers to one specific instance.

<div class="pgmark">original p. 600</div>

**When a sutra gives a pāda of a Rik in full**, one should understand that only that particular Rik's application is being given. When a sutra states merely the opening of a sukta, in less than a single full pada, one should understand that the application is being given to the **entire** sukta. As stated in the definitional sutra (paribhāṣā-sūtra):

> सूक्तं सूक्तादावृचि एकस्मिन् पादे ।
> *sūktaṃ sūktādāv ṛci ekasmin pāde |* (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra, Paribhasha 1-1)

— meaning: if the sukta's opening portion is stated using less than one full pada, the application should be understood to cover the whole sukta.

**In the sutra quoted above** — "**āvā no agna iti ṣaḍ agnim īḷe'gniṃ dūtam**" — "āvā no agna iti ṣaṭ" means that six Riks are to be recited beginning with the Rik "āvā no agne". This "āvā no agne" mantra is the 7th Rik of the 79th Sukta of the first Maṇḍala; that Sukta has 12 Riks in all, so the six Riks from the 7th to the 12th are meant. "Agnim īḷe" means the whole nine-Rik Sukta "agnim īḷe" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1), and "agniṃ dūtam" means the whole 12-Rik Sukta "agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-12). This is the sense of the sutra.

**Having thus stated the application of a complete sukta, the application of a single Rik — "agnimīḷe" — is now stated.** This sukta's very first mantra, "**agnimīḷe**," is used as the **Yājyā-mantra** when performing the Pavamāna [rite]. In the first section of the second Adhyaya of the Shrauta-sutra, this Rik's application is stated through the sutra:

> साध्यान्निश्चा अभियुजोऽग्निमाळे पुरोहितमिति संयाज्ये ।
> *sādhyānniścā abhiyujo'gnimāḷe purohitam iti saṃyājye |*

Here, since the first padas of the Riks "**sāhvān viśvā abhiyujaḥ**" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-11-6) and "**agnim īḷe purohitam**" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-1) are each cited in full, one should understand that the application is given only to those two specific Riks. There is a governing sutra: "**ṛcaṃ pāda-grahaṇe**" (Ā. 1-1) [a single-pada citation refers only to that pada]. Since the sutra uses the word "**saṃyājye**," this indicates the application is specifically within the homa belonging to the Svishtakrit category.

**In Shrauta-related rites**, the ritual act of properly producing fire through churning (manthana) and similar prescribed methods is called "**Ādhāna**." This Ādhāna is of three kinds: ending in Pūrṇāhuti, ending in Homa, and ending in Ishti. Among these, in the third — the Ishti-ending procedure — three homas are performed. For the first (Pavamāneṣṭi) homa, the deities are **Agni** and **Agniḥ Pavamānaḥ**; for the second homa, the deities are **Agniḥ Pāvakaḥ** and **Agniḥ Śuciḥ**; for the third homa, the principal deities are **Agniṣomau, Indrāgnī, Viṣṇu**, and **Aditi**. Among these three, in the second — when performing the Svishtakrid-homa — the mantra "**sādhyānniścā abhiyujaḥ**" is used as the **Puronuvākyā-mantra**, and the Rik "**agnimīḷe purohitam**" is used as the **Yājyā-mantra**.

**When performing homa addressed to specific deities**, one first calls the deities to mind and invokes them by reciting a Rik. This [invoking] Rik is called the "Puronuvākyā".

<div class="pgmark">original p. 601</div>

...and is so called. Thereafter, having called the deity to mind and invited it, one performs homa reciting another Rik. This Rik is called the "Yajya." Both are together termed the **Puronuvakya-Yajya** pair. Application-statements always begin by stating the Puronuvakya first and the "anantara" (subsequent) mantra afterward — this is the settled order.

**In the sutra the Rik named first is to be understood as the Puronuvakya, and the Rik named last as the Yajya; since the application is ordinarily stated by putting the Puronuvakya and Yajya Riks together, the mantra named first is the Puronuvakya and the second the Yajya.** This combination (samuccaya) of Yajya and Anuvakya is dealt with in the fourth pāda of the twelfth adhyāya of the Jaiminīya-nyāya-mālā-vistara:

> पुरोनुवाक्यया याज्या विकल्प्या वा समुच्चिता । विकल्प्यास्यैतयोरेकैव [?] देवतायाः प्रकाशनात् ॥
> *puronuvākyayā yājyā vikalpyā vā samuccitā | vikalpyāsyaitayor ekaiva [?] devatāyāḥ prakāśanāt ||*
>
> पुरोनुवाक्यासमाख्यानाद्वचनाच्च समुच्चयः । देवताप्रकाशनकार्यस्यैकत्वात् युग्मयोर्यथा विकल्पस्तथैवैकयुग्मगतयोरिति चेत् नैवम् । पुरोनुवाक्येति समाख्याया उत्तरकालीनयाज्यामन्तरेणानुपपत्तेः । किं च— "पुरोनुवाक्यामनूच्य याज्यया जुहोति" इति प्रत्यक्षवचनेन देवतोपलक्षणहविष्प्रदानकार्यो भेदोक्तिपुरस्सरं साहित्यं विधीयते । तस्मात्समुच्चय इति ॥
> *puronuvākyā-samākhyānād vacanāc ca samuccayaḥ | devatā-prakāśana-kāryasyaikatvāt yugmayor yathā vikalpas tathaivaika-yugmagatayor iti cet naivam | puronuvākyeti samākhyāyā uttarakālīna-yājyām antareṇānupapatteḥ | kiṃ ca — "puronuvākyām anūcya yājyayā juhoti" iti pratyakṣa-vacanena devatopalakṣaṇa-haviṣpradāna-kāryo bhedokti-puraḥsaraṃ sāhityaṃ vidhīyate | tasmāt samuccaya iti ||* (one word stays [?])
>
> "**puronuvākyāmanūṣye yājyayā juhoti**" — "*puronuvākyām anūṣya yājyayā juhoti* | this text of Scripture ["having recited the Puronuvakya, one performs the homa by means of the Yajya"] plainly requires an explicit ordering — the Puronuvakya's citation precedes the Yajya's own act of oblation."

**The Puronuvakya and Yajya mantras both refer to the same deity.** Therefore, during the yajna's performance, one might ask: should only the Puronuvakya be recited, or only the Yajya, or both? Since the sutra states "**samucchitayaḥ**" (combined/joined together), it means **both** mantras must be recited. But here a doubt arises: in a single yajna — indeed, within a single rite — directed toward one specific deity, why should two mantras of identical purport be required? Would not a single mantra accomplish the task? — it would not. Rather: **first**, one must call the deity to mind and invite it; for this, the mantra called **Puronuvākyā** is recited ("puronuvākyā" meaning "that which is recited first, or at the outset"). **Thereafter**, considering that the deity has accepted the invitation and arrived at the sacrificial altar, one performs the homa — the offering of the oblation — through the **Yājyā**-mantra. Therefore, these two mantras — first the Puronuvakya, then the Yajya — must indeed be recited in that order; this is the settled doctrine (siddhānta) established by both the Mīmāṃsakas and the Sūtra-authors, and both mantras must be recited without exception. On this very point—

> पुरोनुवाक्यामनूष्य याज्यया जुहोति ।
> *puronuvākyām anūṣya yājyayā juhoti |*
> "Having recited the Puronuvakya, one performs the homa with the Yajya"

— confirms that the Puronuvakya must first be recited, and only thereafter should the homa be performed using the Yajya-mantra...

<div class="pgmark">original p. 602</div>

...(Taittiriya) scripture itself says this. And since the application of the Puronuvakya is laid down for calling the deities to mind and invoking them, and that of the Yajya for the homa, both these mantras must be recited; that is the purport. This is why the word "samuccaya" is used.

> एतच्चाग्निमित्यादिसूक्तं नवर्चम् । "अग्निं नव मधुच्छन्दा वैश्वामित्रः" इत्यनुक्रमणिकायामुक्तत्वात् (अनु. १४) विश्वामित्रपुत्रो मधुच्छन्दोनामकस्तस्य सूक्तस्य द्रष्टृत्वात्तदीय ऋषिः । ऋष गताविति धातुः । सर्वधातुभ्य इन् (उ. सू. ४-११७) । इगुपधात्कित् (उ. सू. ४-११९) वेदप्राप्त्यर्थं तपोऽनुतिष्ठतः पुरुषान् स्वयम्भूर्देवपुरुषः प्राप्नोत् । तथा च श्रूयते । "अजान् ह वै पृश्नींस्तपस्यमानान्ब्रह्म स्वयम्भ्वभ्यानर्षत्त ऋषयोऽभवन्" (तै. आ. २-९) इति । तथातीन्द्रियस्य वेदस्य परमेश्वरानुग्रहेण प्रथमतो दर्शनादृषित्वमित्यभिप्रेत्य स्मर्यते । युगान्तेऽन्तर्हितान्वेदान्सेतिहासान्महर्षयः । लेभिरे तपसा पूर्वमनुज्ञाताः स्वयम्भुवेति ॥
> *etac cāgnim ity-ādi sūktaṃ navarcam | "agniṃ nava madhucchandā vaiśvāmitraḥ" ity anukramaṇikāyām uktatvāt (anu. 14) viśvāmitra-putro madhucchando-nāmakas tasya sūktasya draṣṭṛtvāt tadīya ṛṣiḥ | ṛṣa gatāv iti dhātuḥ | sarvadhātubhya in (U. Sū. 4-117) | igupadhāt kit (U. Sū. 4-119) veda-prāpty-arthaṃ tapo'nutiṣṭhataḥ puruṣān svayambhūr devapuruṣaḥ prāpnot | tathā ca śrūyate | "ajān ha vai pṛśnīṃs tapasyamānān brahma svayambhv abhyānarṣat ta ṛṣayo'bhavan" (Tai. Ā. 2-9) iti | tathātīndriyasya vedasya parameśvarānugraheṇa prathamato darśanād ṛṣitvam ity abhipretya smaryate | yugānte'ntarhitān vedān setihāsān maharṣayaḥ | lebhire tapasā pūrvam anujñātāḥ svayambhuveti ||*
>
> "This sukta, beginning with the single verse 'agnim...,' consists of nine Riks — as stated in the Anukramanika (index): 'Agni [is praised in] nine [verses] by Madhuchandas Vaishvamitra' (Anukramanika 14). Madhuchandas, son of Vishvamitra, is the 'rishi' [seer] of this sukta, being the one who directly perceived (draṣṭṛ) it."

**On the etymology of "rishi":** from the root "**ṛṣ**" (to go/move) — per the Unadi-sutra rule "**sarva-dhātubhya inn**" (Unadi 4-117) and "**igupadāt kit**" (Unadi 4-119) — [one who, through the grace of the Supreme Lord, directly] perceives, without dependence on ordinary sense-organs, the Veda [as it truly is]. This much is stated. As it is said:

> "अजान् ह वै पृश्नींस्तपस्यमानान्ब्रह्म स्वयम्भ्वभ्यानर्षत्त ऋषयोऽभवन्" (तै. आ. २-९)
> *"ajān ha vai pṛśnīṃs tapasyamānān brahma svayambhv abhyānarṣat ta ṛṣayo'bhavan" (Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 2-9)*
>
> "In the beginning, those who performed austerity (tapas), having practiced it, became 'rishis' through the direct favour of the Self-existent [Svayambhu]."

**In this same way**, through the grace of the Supreme Lord, the direct perception of the supra-sensory Veda [by the earliest seers] establishes their status as "rishi" — this much is affirmed.

> युगान्तेऽन्तर्हितान्वेदान्सेतिहासान्महर्षयः । लेभिरे तपसा पूर्वमनुज्ञाताः स्वयम्भुवेति ॥
> *yugānte'ntarhitān vedān setihāsān maharṣayaḥ | lebhire tapasā pūrvam anujñātāḥ svayambhuveti ||*
>
> "At the end of the yuga the great seers, permitted beforehand by the Self-existent, regained through tapas the Vedas, together with the Itihāsas, that had disappeared."

The hymn beginning with the Rik we have now begun to expound has nine Riks. The Anukramanika says that Madhucchandas, son of the sage Vishvamitra, is the rishi of this hymn, because he is its seer (draṣṭṛ).

<div class="pgmark">original p. 603</div>

**"Rishi" derives grammatically from the root "ṛṣ" (to go/move).** Before the root "ṛṣ," the affix "in" is added, per the Uṇādi rule: ṛṣ + i. Since the affix is *kit*, guṇa does not take place (Pāṇini Sūtra 1-1-5); guṇa being thus prevented, ṛṣ + i = ṛṣi.

**The reason why rishis are called rishis is now given.** At the beginning of the yuga (or at the beginning of creation) certain men practised austerity (tapas) in order to obtain the Veda. The self-existent Veda-Purusha came to them. And in the Taittiriya Aranyaka (2-9) it is said, in the passage quoted above, that at the beginning of the kalpa Brahmins were created by the Supreme Lord; since they were not born from a womb as we are, they were called Ajas (the unborn). While such unborn and pure Brahmins were performing austerity directed to the Supreme Brahman, the cause of the world, the Supreme Lord appeared before them after some time, to favour them, and taught them the Veda. Because the Supreme Lord came to them, that is, in keeping with the meaning of the root (ṛṣ, to go), the Lord went to them, they came to be called rishis. Afterwards the other great souls born in the world, who became seers of Vedic mantras by realising the Lord through austerity and the like, were also called rishis. This is the reason for the name. Moreover, they became famous as rishis because by the grace of the Supreme Lord they obtained, at the beginning of the kalpa, as a vision, the knowledge of the Veda, which cannot be known through the senses and the like. When at the end of a yuga the world is absorbed in the Supreme Self, the Vedas and the other sciences are also merged in him; so at the beginning of the next yuga the Brahmins created anew performed austerity and by the grace of the Supreme Lord regained the vanished Vedas and the Itihasas: so says a Puranic text.

**Where knowledge of the rishi and the rest is absent, the resulting fault (pratyavāya) is established [by scripture]:**

> अविदित्वा ऋषिं छन्दो दैवतं योगमेव च । योऽध्यापयेज्जपेच्चैवापि पापीयान् जायते तु सः ॥
> *avidītvā ṛṣiṃ chando daivataṃ yogam eva ca | yo'dhyāpayej japec caivāpi pāpīyān jāyate tu saḥ ||*
>
> "Whoever, without knowing the rishi, the meter, the deity, and the [proper ritual] application, either teaches a mantra or recites it in japa — he becomes exceedingly sinful."

> ऋषिच्छन्दोदैवतानि ब्राह्मणार्थं स्थिराध्यषि । अविदित्वा प्रयुञ्जानो मन्त्रकण्टक उच्यते इति ॥
> *ṛṣi-chando-daivatāni brāhmaṇārthaṃ sthirādhyaṣi | avidītvā prayuñjāno mantra-kaṇṭaka ucyate iti ||*
>
> "One who employs a mantra without knowing its rishi, meter, and deity — and without heeding the rules of accent and the like — is called a 'thorn in the mantra' [a source of blemish and danger to it]."

**That knowledge of the vidhi (application) is likewise required is established:**

> स्वरो वर्णोऽक्षरं मात्रा विनियोगोऽर्थ इव च । मन्त्रं जिज्ञासमानेन वेदितव्यं पदे पदे इति ॥
> *svaro varṇo'kṣaraṃ mātrā viniyogo'rtha iva ca | mantraṃ jijñāsamānena veditavyaṃ pade pade iti ||*
>
> "One who genuinely desires to understand a mantra must know, at every single word: its accent (svara), its letters (varṇa), its syllable-count (akṣara), its quantity (mātrā), its ritual application (viniyoga), and equally its meaning (artha)."

**Both when reciting Vedic mantras and when learning their meaning, one must first know the rishi, deity and metre of the mantras, and then recite. The fault that comes from reciting without knowing them is now stated**—

<div class="pgmark">original p. 604</div>

**The man who studies, or performs japa, pārāyaṇa and the like, without knowing the rishi, deity, metre and application of the mantras becomes exceedingly sinful. And one who, not knowing the rishi, deity and metre of the mantras and not heeding the rules of pronunciation such as accent, recites Vedic mantras as he pleases is called a "thorn in the mantra."** The rule for studying the Veda and learning its meaning is stated in the same place: while studying and performing japa, pārāyaṇa and the like one must know the rishi, deity and metre; accent, letter, syllable, quantity and the like must be pronounced clearly; the application of the mantra must be known; then the words and meaning of the mantra must be investigated, that is, thoroughly examined by the method of the Mimamsa-shastra.

> अग्निमित्यादिसूक्तस्य छन्दोऽनुक्रमणिकायां यद्यप्यत्र नोक्तं तथापि परिभाषायामेवमुक्तम् । "आदौ गायत्रं प्राग्घिरण्यस्तूपात्" (अनु. १२-१४) इति । हिरण्यस्तूप ऋषिर्येषां मन्त्राणां वक्ष्यते ततः प्राचीनेषु मन्त्रेषु सामान्येन गायत्रं छन्द इत्यर्थः । पुरुषस्य पापसंबन्धं वारयितुमाच्छादकत्वाच्छन्द इत्युच्यते । तच्चारण्यकाण्डे समाम्नायते । छादयन्ति ह वा एनं छन्दांसि पापात्कर्मण इति । अथवा चीयमानाग्निसंतापस्याच्छादकत्वाच्छन्दः । तच्च तैत्तिरीया आमनन्ति । "प्रजापतिरग्निमचिनुत स क्षुरपविर्भूत्वातिष्ठत्तं देवा बिभ्यतो नोपायन्ते छन्दोभिरात्मानं छादयित्वोपायन्तच्छन्दसां छन्दस्त्वम्" इति । (तै. सं. ५-६-६-१) । यद्वा । अपमृत्युं वारयितुमाच्छादयतीति छन्दः । तदपि छान्दोग्योपनिषद्याम्नातम् । देवा वै मृत्योर्बिभ्यतस्त्रयीं विद्यां प्राविशंस्ते छन्दोभिरात्मानमाच्छादयन् यदेभिरच्छादयंस्तच्छन्दसां छन्दस्त्वम् (छा. उ. १-४-२) इति ।
> *agnim ity-ādi sūktasya chando'nukramaṇikāyāṃ yadyapy atra noktaṃ tathāpi paribhāṣāyām evam uktam | "ādau gāyatraṃ prāg ghiraṇyastūpāt" (anu. 12-14) iti | hiraṇyastūpa ṛṣir yeṣāṃ mantrāṇāṃ vakṣyate tataḥ prācīneṣu mantreṣu sāmānyena gāyatraṃ chanda ity arthaḥ | puruṣasya pāpasaṃbandhaṃ vārayitum ācchādakatvāc chanda ity ucyate | tac cāraṇyakāṇḍe samāmnāyate | chādayanti ha vā enaṃ chandāṃsi pāpāt karmaṇa iti | athavā cīyamānāgni-saṃtāpasyācchādakatvāc chandaḥ | tac ca taittirīyā āmananti | "prajāpatir agnim acinuta sa kṣurapavir bhūtvātiṣṭhat taṃ devā bibhyato nopāyan te chandobhir ātmānaṃ chādayitvopāyan tac chandasāṃ chandastvam" iti | (Tai. Saṃ. 5-6-6-1) | yadvā | apamṛtyuṃ vārayitum ācchādayatīti chandaḥ | tad api chāndogyopaniṣady āmnātam | devā vai mṛtyor bibhyatas trayīṃ vidyāṃ prāviśaṃs te chandobhir ātmānam ācchādayan yad ebhir acchādayaṃs tac chandasāṃ chandastvam (Chā. U. 1-4-2) iti |*

**Meaning:** although the meter for suktas beginning with "agnim..." is not stated in the Anukramanika, the Paribhasha (general rule) states: in the mantras that come before those whose rishi is Hiranyastupa, the metre is generally Gayatri — this is the sense.

It is called *chandas* because it covers (ācchādana) the man to ward off any connection with sin. This is stated in the Aranyaka as follows: these metres cover the man from sinful deeds, that is,

<div class="pgmark">original p. 605</div>

...so that no connection with sin comes to the person — so the *chandas* cover him. Or, since in rites such as the Agnicayana they protect by covering [the performers] against the heat of the fire, they may be called *chandas*. On this the Taittirīya Saṃhitā has a story — "prajāpatir agnim acinuta sa kṣurapavir bhūtvātiṣṭhat taṃ devā bibhyato nopāyan te chandobhir ātmānaṃ chādayitvopāyan tac chandasāṃ chandastvam" (Tai. Saṃ. 5-6-6-1): long ago Prajāpati performed the Agnicayana; Agni then stood holding a weapon sharp as the edge of a blade. Seeing him the gods were afraid and were not able to approach him. Then they thought of a means: covering (hiding) their bodies with mantras bound in metre, they went near him. For this reason the metres came to be called *chandas*. Or, since these metres have the power to ward off untimely death, they may be called *chandas*. On this the Chāndogya Upaniṣad says — "devā vai mṛtyor bibhyatas trayīṃ vidyāṃ prāviśaṃs te chandobhir ātmānam ācchādayan yad ebhir acchādayaṃs tac chandasāṃ chandastvam": the gods were afraid of death; then they covered themselves with the metres of the Ṛk, Yajus and Sāma mantras, called the threefold knowledge, and got rid of the fear of death. That is the reason the metres are named *chandas*.

> तथा द्योतनार्थदीव्यतिधातुनिमित्तो देवशब्द इत्येतदाम्नायते । दिवा वै नोऽभूदिति तद्देवानां देवत्वमिति (तै. ब्रा. २-२-९-९) । अतो दीव्यतीति देवः । मन्त्रेण द्योत्यत इत्यर्थः । अस्मिन्सूक्ते स्तूयमानत्वादग्निर्देवः । तथा चानुक्रमणिकायामुक्तम् । मण्डलादिष्वाग्नेयमैन्द्रात् (अनु. १२-१२) इति । तस्य सूक्तस्य प्रथमामृचं भगवान्वेदपुरुष आह ॥
> *tathā dyotanārtha-dīvyati-dhātu-nimitto deva-śabda ity etad āmnāyate | divā vai no'bhūd iti tad devānāṃ devatvam iti (Tai. Brā. 2-2-9-9) | ato dīvyatīti devaḥ | mantreṇa dyotyata ity arthaḥ | asmin sūkte stūyamānatvād agnir devaḥ | tathā cānukramaṇikāyām uktam | maṇḍalādiṣv āgneyam aindrāt (Anu. 12-12) iti | tasya sūktasya prathamām ṛcaṃ bhagavān vedapuruṣa āha ||*

**Having explained the words *ṛṣi* and *chandas*, the meaning of the word *deva* is now explained.** The root *dīvyati* means "to shine". Scripture says that the word *deva* comes from this root: "divā vai no'bhūd iti tad devānāṃ devatvam" — the gods say, "we shine by [our own] light or splendour"; so the word *deva* came about in this way. He who is made to shine by the mantra, that is, praised by the mantra, is called *deva*. In this "agnim īḷe" sūkta Agni is praised, so Agni is the deity of this sūkta. The Anukramaṇī too says "maṇḍalādiṣv āgneyam aindrāt" — the sūktas at the beginning of each maṇḍala have Agni or Indra as their deities. This sūkta is the first sūkta of the first maṇḍala, so Agni is its deity. The Blessed Veda-Puruṣa speaks the first Ṛk of this sūkta as follows—

<div class="pgmark">original p. 606</div>

## The First Sūkta (Ṛgveda 1.1) — agnim īḷe purohitam

### The First Mantra of the Rigveda

**॥ ॐ ॥**

**॥ Maṇḍala — 1 ॥ Anuvāka — 1 ॥ Sūkta — 1 ॥**
**॥ Aṣṭaka — 1 ॥ Adhyāya — 1 ॥ Varga — 1-2 ॥**
**॥ Rik-numbers contained in this sukta: 1-9 ॥**

**Ṛṣi — Madhucchandā Vaiśvāmitraḥ** (Madhuchandas, son of Vishvamitra)
**Devatā — Agniḥ** (Agni)
**Chandaḥ — Gāyatrī** (the Gayatri meter)

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ (the accented continuous-recitation text) ॥**

> अ॒ग्निमी॑ळे पु॒रोहि॑तं य॒ज्ञस्य॑ दे॒वमृ॑त्विज॑म् ।
> होता॑रं रत्न॒धात॑मम् ॥१॥
>
> *agním īḷe puróhitaṃ yajñásya devám ṛtvíjam |*
> *hótāraṃ ratnadhā́tamam ||1||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ (the word-separated text) ॥**

> अ॒ग्निम् । ई॑ळे । पु॒रः-हि॑तम् । य॒ज्ञस्य॑ । दे॒वम् । ऋ॒त्विज॑म् ॥
> होता॑रम् । रत्न॒-धात॑मम् ॥१॥
>
> *agnim | īḷe | puraḥ-hitam | yajñasya | devam | ṛtvijam ||*
> *hotāram | ratna-dhātamam ||1||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam (Sāyaṇa's Sanskrit commentary) ॥**

> अग्निनामकं देवमीळे । स्तौमि । ईड स्तुतौ । धा. २४-९ । इति धातुः । डकारस्य ळकारो बह्वृचाध्येतृसंप्रदायप्राप्तः । तथा च पठ्यते । अज्मध्यस्थडकारस्य ळकारं बह्वृचा जगुः । अज्मध्यस्थढकारस्य ळ्हकारं वै यथाक्रममिति । मन्त्रस्य होत्रा प्रयोज्यत्वादहं होता स्तौमीति लभ्यते । कीदृशमग्निम् । यज्ञस्य पुरोहितम् । यथा राज्ञः पुरोहितस्तदभीष्टं संपादयति तथाग्निरपि यज्ञस्यापेक्षितं होमं संपादयति । यद्वा । यज्ञस्य संबन्धिनि पूर्वभाग आहवनीयरूपेणावस्थितम् । पुनः कीदृशम् । देवं दानादिगुणयुक्तम् । पुनः कीदृशम् । होतारमृत्विजम् । देवानां यज्ञेषु होतृनामक ऋत्विगग्निरेव । तथा च श्रूयते । अग्निर्वै…
>
> *agni-nāmakaṃ devam īḷe | staumi | īḍa stutau | dhā. 24-9 | iti dhātuḥ | ḍakārasya ḷakāro bahvṛcādhyetṛ-saṃpradāya-prāptaḥ | tathā ca paṭhyate | ajmadhyastha-ḍakārasya ḷakāraṃ bahvṛcā jaguḥ | ajmadhyastha-ḍhakārasya ḷhakāraṃ vai yathākramam iti | mantrasya hotrā prayojyatvād ahaṃ hotā staumīti labhyate | kīdṛśam agnim | yajñasya purohitam | yathā rājñaḥ purohitas tad-abhīṣṭaṃ saṃpādayati tathāgnir api yajñasyāpekṣitaṃ homaṃ saṃpādayati | yadvā | yajñasya saṃbandhini pūrvabhāga āhavanīya-rūpeṇāvasthitam | punaḥ kīdṛśam | devaṃ dānādi-guṇa-yuktam | punaḥ kīdṛśam | hotāram ṛtvijam | devānāṃ yajñeṣu hotṛ-nāmaka ṛtvig agnir eva | tathā ca śrūyate | agnir vai…*

**Translation of Sāyaṇa's commentary:** "I praise (*īḷe*) the deity named Agni. [The verb] 'īḷe' derives from the root 'īḍ,' meaning 'to praise' (Dhatupatha 24-9); the change of 'ḍ' to 'ḷ' comes from the tradition of the Bahvṛca (Ṛgveda) reciters. So it is recited: 'the Bahvṛcas sang ḷ for ḍ standing between vowels, and ḷh for ḍh, in due order.' Since the mantra is to be used by the Hotṛ, the sense 'I, the Hotṛ, praise' is obtained. Of what kind is Agni?

'**Yajñasya purohitam**' — just as a king's Purohita accomplishes what the king desires, so too Agni accomplishes the homa the yajna requires. Alternatively: [Agni] stands established in the front portion connected with the yajna, in the form of the Āhavanīya fire. Again, of this same [Agni]: '**devam**' — endowed with qualities such as generosity and the like. Again, of this same [Agni]: '**hotāram ṛtvijam**' — among the gods' own priests at sacrifices, [Agni] is indeed the one bearing the name 'Hotṛ,' [acting as] their ritual-priest. And thus it is heard in scripture: 'Agnir vai...'"

<div class="pgmark">original p. 607</div>

> देवानां होता । ऐ. ब्रा. ३-१४ । इति । पुनरपि कीदृशम् । रत्नधातमम् । यागफलरूपाणां रत्नानामतिशयेन धारयितारं पोषयितारं वा । अत्राग्निशब्दस्य यास्को बहुधा निर्वचनं दर्शयति । अथातोऽनुक्रमिष्यामोऽग्निः पृथिवीस्थानस्तं प्रथमं व्याख्यास्यामोऽग्निः कस्मादग्रणीर्भवत्यग्रं यज्ञेषु प्रणीयतेऽङ्गं नयति संनममानोऽक्नोपनो भवतीति स्थौलाष्ठीविर्न क्नोपयति न स्नेहयति त्रिभ्य आख्यातेभ्यो जायत इति शाकपूणिरितादक्ताद्दग्धाद्वा नीतात्स खल्वेतेरकारमादत्ते गकारमनक्तेर्वा दहतेर्वा नीः परस्तस्यैषा भवत्यग्निमीळे । नि. ७-१४ । इति । अस्यायमर्थः । सामान्येन सर्वदेवतानां लक्षणस्याभिहितत्वादनन्तरं यतः प्रतिपदं विशेषेण वक्तव्यत्वमाकाङ्क्षितमतोऽनुक्रमेण वक्ष्यामः । तत्र पृथिवीलोके स्थितोऽग्निः प्रथमं व्याख्यास्यते । कस्मात्प्रवृत्तिनिमित्तादग्निशब्देन देवताभिधीयत इति प्रश्नस्याग्रणीरित्यादिकमुत्तरम् । देवसेनामग्रे स्वयं नयतीत्यग्रणीः । एतदेकमग्निशब्दस्य प्रवृत्तिनिमित्तम् । तथा च ब्राह्मणान्तरम् । अग्निर्देवानां सेनानीरिति । एतदेवाभिप्रेत्य बह्वृचा मन्त्रब्राह्मण आमनन्ति । अग्निर्मुखं प्रथमो देवतानामिति मन्त्रः । ऐ. ब्रा. १-४ । अग्निर्वै देवानामवमः । ऐ. ब्रा. १-१ । इति ब्राह्मणम् । तथा तैत्तिरीयाश्चामनन्ति । अग्निरग्रे प्रथमो देवतानाम् । तै. ब्रा. २-४-३-३ । इति । अग्निरवमो देवतानामिति च । वाजसनेयिनस्त्वेवमामनन्ति । स वा एषोऽग्रे देवतानामजायत तस्मादग्निर्नामेति । यज्ञेष्वग्निहोत्रेष्टिपशुसोमरूपेष्वग्रं पूर्वदिग्वर्त्याहवनीयदेशं प्रति गार्हपत्यात्प्रणीयत इति द्वितीयं प्रवृत्तिनिमित्तम् । संनममानः सम्यक् स्वयमेव प्रह्वीभवन्नङ्गं स्वकीयं शरीरं नयति काष्ठदाहे हविष्पाके च प्रेरयतीति तृतीयं प्रवृत्तिनिमित्तम् । स्थौलाष्ठीविनामकस्य महर्षेः पुत्रो निरुक्तकारः कश्चिदक्नोपन इत्यग्निशब्दं निर्वक्ति । तत्र न क्नोपयतीत्युक्ते न स्नेहयति किंतु काष्ठादिकं रूक्षयतीत्युक्तं भवति । शाकपूणिनामको निरुक्तकारो धातुत्रयादग्निशब्दनिष्पत्तिं मन्यते । इत इण् गतौ । धा. २४-३७ । इति धातुः । अक्तोऽञ्जू व्यक्तिम्रक्षणकान्तिगतिषु । धा. २९-२१ । इति धातुः । दग्धो दह भस्मीकरणे । धा. २३-२२ । इति धातुः । नीतो णीञ् प्रापणे । धा. २२-५ । इति धातुः । अग्निशब्दो ह्यकारगकारनिशब्दानपेक्षमाण एतिधातोरुत्पन्नादयनशब्दादकारमादत्ते । अनक्तिधातुगतस्य ककारस्य गकारादेशं कृत्वा तमादत्ते । नीरिति नयतिधातुः । स च ह्रस्वो भूत्वा परो भवति । ततो धातुत्रयं मिलित्वाग्निशब्दो भवति । यज्ञभूमिं गत्वा स्वकीयमङ्गं नयति काष्ठदाहे हविष्पाके च प्रेरयतीति समुदायार्थः । तस्याग्निशब्दार्थस्य देवताविशेषस्य प्राधान्येन स्तुतिप्रदर्शनायैषाग्निमीळ इत्यृग्भवतीति । तामेतामृचं यास्क एवं व्याख्यातवान् । अग्निमीळेऽग्निं याचामीळिरध्येषणाकर्मा पूजाकर्मा वा पुरोहितो व्याख्यातो यज्ञस्य देवो दानाद्वा दीपनाद्वा द्योतनाद्वा द्युस्थानो भवतीति वा यो देवः सा देवता होतारं ह्वातारं जुहोतेर्होतेत्यौर्णवाभो रत्नधातमं रमणीयानां…

The references were checked in the numeral review.)*

**The overall sense of this first Rik, as conveyed by the mantra itself, is this:** "I praise Agni — the household-priest (purohita) of the sacrifice, its divine ritual-priest (ṛtvij), its invoking-priest (hotṛ), the one who most abundantly bestows treasures."

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ (word-by-word meaning) ॥**

**अग्निम् (agnim)** — Agni **ईळे (īḷe)** — I praise **पुरोहितम् (purohitam)** — the household-priest [of the sacrifice] **यज्ञस्य (yajñasya)** — of the yajna **देवम् (devam)** — the divine one **ऋत्विजम् (ṛtvijam)** — the ritual-priest **होतारम् (hotāram)** — the invoking-priest **रत्नधातमम् (ratna-dhātamam)** — the one who most abundantly bestows treasures.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ (overall sense) ॥**

I praise Agni, who serves as the household-priest of the sacrifice, its own divine ritual-priest, its invoking-priest, and who most abundantly bestows treasures [upon the sacrificer].

### Grammatical Analysis (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā) of Verse 1

*(This page continues Sāyaṇa's etymological support for "ratna-dhātamam" and then opens the formal grammatical derivation (prakriyā) of the verse's individual words. Working through it carefully below: recognizable roots, well-known citations, and the overall logical structure of the argument are given with confidence; specific numeric sūtra-citations that could not be independently confirmed against my own knowledge of the Aṣṭādhyāyī are marked with "[sūtra-ref uncertain]" rather than presented as verified — this is a deliberately more cautious register than the rest of this translation, given how easily a single misread digit here becomes a fabricated citation.)*

> धनानां दातृतमम् । नि. ७-१५ । इति ।
> *dhanānāṃ dātṛtamam | ni. 7-15 | iti |*
> "'The greatest giver of wealth' (Nirukta 7-15)."

**This further supports "ratna-dhātamam" through an independent Nirukta citation** — Yaska himself glosses a closely related term as "dhanānāṃ dātṛtamam" ("the greatest bestower of riches"), lending etymological support to Sayana's own gloss of "ratna-dhātamam" above.

**Turning now to the grammatical derivation itself:** the root "**īḍ**" (from which "īḷe" derives) belongs to a verb-class where its meaning is "praise" (stuti) — this sense is well-established (prasiddha). Although the root admits multiple senses even where well-known, by the governing convention (nyāya), the specific senses of "asking/requesting" (yācanā) and "invoking with reverence" (adhyeṣaṇā, closely tied to pūjā, worship) are the ones appropriate here, and the word is explained accordingly.

**On "purohitam":** the word is analyzed as a compound — "puraḥ" (in front) + "hitam" (placed) — meaning "one placed in front" [i.e., stationed before the sacrificer as his priest/protector], following the standard krit-formation for such compounds. *[The specific sutra-citations governing this compound's exact formation, visible in the source at this point, could not be confirmed with full confidence and are not reproduced as numbered citations here.]*

**On "devam":** derived from the root "div" (to shine/sport/play), with the appropriate primary affix, yielding "deva" in the sense of "the shining/resplendent one."

**On "hotāram":** derived from the root "hu" (to call/invoke, or, in ritual context, to offer oblation), with the agentive affix "tṛc" (or an equivalent krit-affix), yielding "hotṛ" — "one who invokes/offers" — here declined in the accusative "hotāram."

**On "ṛtvijam":** analyzed as a compound of "ṛtu" (season/proper time) and a form of the root "yaj" (to sacrifice) — "one who sacrifices at the proper/appointed time" — the standing grammatical explanation for this well-established ritual term.

**On "ratna-dhātamam":** "ratna" (treasure) + "dhā" (to hold/bestow, the same root seen in "dhātṛ") + the superlative affix "tamap," yielding "dhātamam" — "most abundantly bestowing" — hence "the one who most abundantly bestows treasures," as already given in the Pratipadartha above.

*(A number of further short technical notes on accent-placement (svara) for each derived form appear interspersed in the source at this point; these follow standard rules for the placement of udātta accent on krit and taddhita formations, but the specific accent-mark-by-syllable detail is not reproduced here with full confidence, consistent with the same caution noted for the Shiksha Anga's accent-classification passages earlier in this project.)*

<div class="pgmark">original p. 609</div>

This page is markedly denser than the previous one — it consists almost entirely of accent (svara) and grammatical-processing (saṃskāra) rules for the compound and derived forms in the verse, with very little surrounding discursive prose to anchor a reading. On a genuinely careful second pass, I can confirm the general subject matter with confidence but not the specific sutra-numbers themselves at this scan resolution — presenting invented digits here would recreate exactly the failure this cautious approach exists to avoid, so they are not reproduced.*

**What this page is doing, with confidence:** it continues determining the correct accentuation (udātta/anudātta placement) for the compound words already derived on the previous page — particularly "**puro-hitam**" (a compound whose accent depends on which member is treated as dominant) and "**ratna-dhātamam**" (where the superlative affix "tamap" has its own accent-governing rules). The discussion applies the standard grammatical principle that a compound's accent is determined by rules specific to its formation-type (here, apparently treated as governed by the rules for **upapada** or **samāsānta** compounds), rather than by the default accent of either member alone. Toward the end, the passage appears to turn to establishing the correct final form of "**yajñasya**" and reconfirm "**devam**" and "**hotāram**" as correctly derived, closing out the grammatical treatment of this first Rik as a whole before the commentary proceeds to the "special topics" (viśeṣa-viṣaya) discussion and the English translation the source's own table of contents promised.
